pages.text: A chassis has six faces named from its own point of view: **F**ront, Bac**K**, **L**eft, **R**ight, **T**op, **B**ottom. The front carries a copper chevron. Turning the chassis turns the whole machine: modules keep their local faces.

**One face, one module.** Service bays only add capacity or throughput; they never add faces or functions. Every way in or out of a chassis draws from the same per-tick budgets, so six ports cannot each move the full amount.

An empty face exposes nothing to its neighbour, and nothing is exposed to side-less queries. Breaking a chassis drops its modules, upgrades and lane items once; **fluid and stored RF are lost**.
